The hypothesis was that increased you know sleep would improve test performance but results did not fully confirm that. We had a sample of 30 students split into 2 groups and the control group slept normally while the treatment group got an extra 2 hours.

The average score in the treatment group was 84 compared to 79 in the control group which is a difference of 5 points.

The p value was 0.04 which is significant at the 5% level but the effect size is modest. one limitation is that we did not control for caffeine intake which could have affected the results.

The next study should use a larger sample and measure sleep quality more directly.
